title: Whole-system normalization of recursive coefficient transport
statement: Fix normalized transport data [def-pur-completed-coefficient-family-transport-models] and the recursive complete evaluations, their ambient identification, and recursive a/b transport $e_P$ [def-pur-completed-coefficient-transport-expressions]. Use the whole-system expression comparisons $\beta_P$, their coherent reductions $\gamma_P$ and their structural evaluation [def-pur-completed-operation-comparison-data]. For a normalized input family $N$, let $M_i=\mathcal L N_i$ with its specified completeness. Define the constant-side system comparison recursively. At an input it is identity; at a coefficient unit it is the coefficient-unit transport followed by the unit identification. At a tensor vertex apply ordinary constant tensor to the two recursive maps, then the representative-normalized balancing map, the actual R-completion unit and the coherent-counit tensor comparison; extend this map through constant completion using the inverse reflector Hom bijection. At a pullback vertex apply ordinary constant inverse image to the recursive map, then the scalar-unit mate $\tau$, the actual R-completion unit, normalized pullback identification and coherent-counit pullback comparison; again extend by that same reflector bijection. Thus the finite constant/completed comparisons are those fixed by the whole strict quotient-tower balancing and scalar-unit representative equations, with all transitions retained. Define ExpressionSystemLaw to require that $e_P$, followed by restriction of the recursive ambient identification and $\beta_P$, equals this constant-side system comparison for every normalized family and expression. Define ExpressionSystemStructuralLaw to require that the actual complete R structural maps, transported by the recursive ambient identifications, satisfy both the total-limit square with $\beta$ and the whole-system reduction square with $\gamma$. These are explicit constructions and predicates, without an existence assertion.
